newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chubais says he is not yet in government.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chubais says he is not yet in government.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's liberal aide, Anatoly Chubais, said on Thursday the Russian leader had not taken a final decision on his transfer to a key post in the government, widely predicted by the media.

"The president has not taken a decision yet," Chubais told reporters after the 66-year-old president delivered a state of the nation address to parliament in which he vowed to restore order, crack down on crime and graft and continue reforms.

Kremlin sources and the Russian media have widely predicted that Yeltsin will make Chubais, now head of his administration, sole first deputy prime minister with wide powers to fight economic crime and pursue reforms.
Many expected this announcement at an expanded government meeting which starts at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) on Thursday.

Chubais, 41, an outstanding administrator, is popular with foreign investors but hated by the communists who dominate parliament and who accuse him of selling firms off cheap in his management of Russia's privatisation drive.
The opposition also hates Chubais for his pivotal role in Yeltsin's re-election campaign last year.
